name: Webhook
description: Receive webhooks from any service by configuring a custom webhook.

block.name: Webhook
block.description: Receive webhooks from any service by configuring a custom webhook.
block.bestPractices:
- You can test the webhook by sending a request to the webhook URL. E.g. depending on authorization: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/trigger/{webhookId} -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Sim-Secret: 1234" -d '{"message": "Test webhook trigger", "data": {"key": "v"}}'
- Continuing example above, the body can be accessed in downstream block using dot notation. E.g. <webhook1.message> and <webhook1.data.key>
- Only use when there's no existing integration for the service with triggerAllowed flag set to true.

triggers.name: Generic Webhook
triggers.description: Receive webhooks from any service or API

credentials.label: Authentication Token
credentials.description: Token used to authenticate webhook requests via Bearer token or custom header

triggers.instructions:
1. Copy the webhook URL and use it in your external service.
2. Configure your service to send webhooks to this URL.
3. If authentication is enabled, include the token in requests using the custom header or Authorization: Bearer TOKEN.
